The given equations represent the squared distances between three points in the plane:
\(d_{12}^2 = 9\), \(d_{13}^2 = 16\), \(d_{23}^2 = 25\).
The side lengths of the triangle are \(3\), \(4\), and \(5\). Since \(3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2\), the triangle is a right triangle with legs \(3\) and \(4\). Its area is \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6\).

The determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\) equals twice the signed area of the triangle. Its absolute value is \(2 \times 6 = 12\). Squaring this gives \(144\).

Answer: 144
